title: CTMRG as a tensor-network message-passing algorithm
abstract: We formulate the corner transfer matrix equations, and the corner transfer matrix renormalization group built on them, as a set of local equations on general planar graphs. These equations depend only on the local subgraphs of the planar graph and are glued together consistently to describe the whole graph. Solving them yields message tensors and corner matrices, which can be used to construct an MPS environment for any connected subgraph. We test the proposed equations on the ferromagnetic Ising model, on a variety of infinite lattices (including hyperbolic ones) and on finite graphs, and find systematic improvement over belief propagation.
summary: This paper develops a unified message-passing framework to compute tensor network contractions, specifically reformulating the Corner Transfer Matrix Renormalization Group (CTMRG). By treating CTMRG as a message-passing algorithm on general planar graphs, it provides a systematic method that unifies previous, case-specific techniques. This advances the computational analysis of 2D statistical mechanics models on complex geometries.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computationally challenging problem of exactly contracting tensor networks defined on two-dimensional planar graphs.
main_result: It successfully formulates the Corner Transfer Matrix Renormalization Group (CTMRG) as a systematic message-passing algorithm analogous to Belief Propagation (BP) for general planar graphs.
method: The method involves defining message tensors and 'corner' matrices that encode local information, establishing self-consistency equations for these tensors by ensuring consistency across shared faces.
model_or_system: The theory is tested on the ferromagnetic Ising model and generalized to arbitrary planar graphs, including those with hyperbolic geometry.
key_observables: The partition function, correlation functions, and the message tensors/corner matrices themselves are the primary focus.
important_parameters: The virtual bond dimension ($\chi$) is a key parameter, with the Belief Propagation limit corresponding to $\chi=1$.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes the existence of a gauge condition for every polygon face to simplify the structure of the corner matrices.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the placement of tensors on vertices and dual graphs, define the message MPS environment, and show the derivation of the universal product form for the CTM equations and the biorthogonal projectors.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the tensor network setup, then introducing the message-passing framework using corner matrices, deriving the self-consistency equations for these matrices, and finally showing how these equations fully determine the message MPS.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the message-passing formalism developed here (reconciling CTMRG and BP) provides a powerful, systematic computational tool applicable to quantum many-body systems described by tensor networks, which is relevant for simulating quantum Hamiltonians.
